issues: standard of review applicable to a spousal sponsorship genuineness determination

whether a sponsor's prior marriages and sponsorship history, including a prior refusal on marriage-of-convenience grounds, is a relevant consideration in assessing the genuineness of a current spousal relationship
whether an officer may rely on the parties' demeanour and body language as evidence of the genuineness of a spousal relationship
whether an officer's apparent pre-judgment or bias vitiates a spousal sponsorship decision on procedural fairness grounds
whether the birth of a child to the couple is dispositive or a strong indicator of the genuineness of the spousal relationship
whether inconsistencies in the parties' testimony are sufficient to find the relationship not genuine, or whether the officer must consider the totality of the evidence
the officer's duty to provide reasons that permit meaningful judicial review of a spousal sponsorship refusal
key_facts: spousal sponsorship application refused on genuineness grounds
sponsor has a history of multiple marriages to women from the same country of origin
one prior sponsorship application was refused on marriage-of-convenience grounds
officer relied on inconsistencies in the parties' testimony
officer relied on demeanour and body language
officer relied on the sponsor's marital and sponsorship history
the couple has a baby daughter together
clients allege the officer had pre-judged the outcome before the interview
clients allege they were treated as criminals during the interview
causes_of_action: judicial review of a spousal sponsorship refusal
